items.title: Brotli / Node.js Vulnerabilities
items.summary: On October 22, 2026, Open AI security researchers announced a critical severity vulnerability in Google’s Brotli decoder, identified as CVE-2026-111497.

items.title: Why U.S. Islands Are Important for Biodiversity
items.summary: Along with the more well-known islands like the Aleutian and Hawaiian Islands, the United States is home to thousands of islands found much closer to the mainland, scattered along coastlines, tucked inside estuaries, and forming barrier islands that separate coastal wetlands from the open ocean .

items.title: How to Use MPKX Files in QGIS
items.summary: With so many public agencies, particularly in the United States, relying almost exclusively on Esri’s proprietary GIS software, it’s not uncommon to find geographic data packaged or compressed in formats designed for ArcGIS.

items.title: GIS File Formats
items.summary: GIS work involves dozens of file formats. Some store geographic data, while others are created by GIS software to save a map or project.

items.title: Anthropic announces closing of initial public offering, including full exercise of underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares, and closing of concurrent private placement
items.summary: Today Anthropic, PBC announced the closing of its initial public offering of an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at a public offering price of $83.00 per share, including the full exercise by the underwriters of their option to purchase an additional 147,000,000 shares of Class A common stock from Anthropic at the initial public offering price.

items.title: Can AI help scientists identify promising drug candidates?

items.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
items.summary: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.
